description: GEER - Croatia is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "field recon", published or maintained by Ingrid Tomac, University of California San Diego (ucsd.edu). This project documents an extensive sinkhole collapse that followed the Mw6.4 earthquake in Croatia. The sinkholes collapsed in a small area of two villages, where karstic rock underlays thick clayey sediments. Coverage: Petrinja, Croatia. DesignSafe files it as a "field recon" project. Keywords: earthquake, sinkholes, liquefaction, infrastructure damage. Published 2022-05-08. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
